claims.evidence: The Azure Architecture Center page Understand data models and the Redis eviction and persistence pages were read from clones of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center and redis/docs at pinned commits; the memory-limit results were measured by the author, who ran them on Redis 7.0.15 with redis-py 8.1.0 on 2026-10-18.

mobile.evidence: Chromium (Playwright) rendered lesson.md (markdown-it, tables enabled, every <details> open, a 16 px page gutter) at each width: the page never scrolled sideways and the figure was scaled to the column; the smallest SVG font-size times that scale is the recorded minimum at 320 px. `python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser` measured every line of the figure in Chromium inside its box. Not GitHub, not a real phone and not learner testing.

claims.claim_vi: Relational stores give multi-row transactional consistency, joins and constraints, and horizontal scale generally requires sharding or partitioning; document stores hold semi-structured JSON with per-document schema flexibility, typical datum size small to medium, and large denormalized documents create partial update contention; column-family stores suit wide, sparse, write-heavy data and need up-front row key design, while massive historical analytical scans go to analytics or OLAP stores; graph stores hold nodes and edges that both carry properties and suit variable-depth traversals; time-series stores are append-oriented with time-window queries and tag cardinality concerns; object stores hold large binaries whose metadata rarely changes; one service may offer several models.
claims.section: Model sections; Comparative characteristics; Choose among models; When to re-evaluate
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center at commit 8e2c239344ee753a88856800b4210a3e27ac1036.

claims.claim_vi: maxmemory limits memory for the dataset and 0 (no limit) is the default on 64-bit systems; noeviction returns an error on writes when the limit is reached; allkeys-lru evicts the least recently used keys; Redis persists with RDB snapshots, an AOF log of every write, both, or none.
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of redis/docs at commit 3b030c7ef066c0bb7f88ddec02c784e49783b0f8.

claims.claim_vi: Measured: with maxmemory 8 MiB and 20,000 values of 1,000 bytes, noeviction accepted 6,732 writes, refused the next with 'OOM command not allowed when used memory > maxmemory' and kept the first key; allkeys-lru accepted all 20,000 writes, kept 6,709 keys, evicted 13,291 and lost the first key.
claims.verified_by: The author ran and measured this on 2026-10-18 on Redis 7.0.15.

claims.claim_vi: The source states: Six database types in one sentence each: relational solves almost anything; in-memory stores are fast with limited data size; time-series stores manage time-stamped data; graph databases suit complex relationships between unstructured objects; document stores are good for large immutable data; wide column stores serve big data, analytics and reporting with denormalized data; the list of databases includes S3 and Ceph. The lesson corrects the graph, document and wide column sentences (see source_deviations).

design_notes_vi: Hai nhóm ba thẻ (câu giữ được, câu cần sửa) và bốn bước thử Redis chạm trần bộ nhớ. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: The source says document stores are good for large immutable data; the lesson follows the Azure guide (small to medium documents that are updated) and assigns large immutable data to object stores.

The source calls graph objects unstructured and puts analytics under wide column stores; the lesson notes that nodes and edges carry properties and that the Azure guide puts large analytical scans in a separate analytics model.
editorial_note_vi: Bài mới viết trong kho này, chờ review kỹ thuật. Chưa user testing hoặc phê duyệt phát hành.
